page.layout: One main text column, wide, with a narrow column of marginal notes at its right edge. Below the text: signature at left, catchword at right. Running head at top. Within the text column: prose paragraphs, a three-line Arabic verse with a Latin translation below it, then the prose continues.

main_text.l: filiam Iorhamidæ, qui cùm ob stuprum in Caaba commissum
à Deo in lapides conversi essent, à Koraishitis
hoc sceleris pretium tulerunt, ut pro Diis haberentur.
Idola hæc ab Amro dedicata imperante Persis Saburo,
seu Sapore Dil Estaf, ac demum sub Mohammede
novæ sectæ conditore, abolita asserit Sharestanius ;
quem tamen eo erroris arguit AbulFeda quòd Amrus
cultûs Idololarrici author, multis ante Saporem eti-
am primum qui Dil'Estafo multo antiquior, sæculis
floruerit. Atque hæc præcipuæ apud Arabes famæ
Idola. Alia se inter legendum offerunt nomine tenus,
non pauca. Ex his سعد Saad, à Bani Malcan, Ebn Cana-
na cultus, teste Sharestanio, &c. de cujus numine re-
ctiùs quàm populares suos judicâsse apud ipsos Poë-
tam, patet ex hoc ipsius carmine

l.i: اتينا الي سعد[?] ليجمع شملنا[?] / فشتتنا سعد[?] فلا نحن من سعد[?] / وهل سعد[?] الا صخرة بتنوفة[?] / من الارض لا تنعوا[?] لغي[?] ولا رشد[?]
i.c. Venimus ad Saadum ut res nostras colligeret, /
At dispersit nos Saadus, nec sumus nos à Saado. /
Quid enim aliud est Saadis quam Petra in deserto, /
E terrâ, quæ nec ad falsum nec ad verum invitat ?

main_text.l: Juxta thematis rationem, prosperitatem sonat nomen,
cùm tamen, ut rectè censuit Poëta, cultoribus suis
non nisi miseriæ causa fuerit. Fuisse autem Idolum
hoc حجرة طويلة[?] i. e. Petram seu Saxum oblongum ad
littus جدة[?] Jodda testatur Safioddinus ab eodem the-
mate سعيدة[?] Saidah, nomen fuisse domus ad quam
peregrinationes instituere soliti Arabes testantur,
idem

page.notes: Arabic verse and Arabic inline words: transcribed from a small, faint scan; the vowel-less letters are uncertain and each doubtful word is marked [?]. Italics for proper names and the Latin verse are approximated from the scan. The Arabic verse is set as one stanza, its four lines separated by " / ". The Latin verse is one stanza, lines separated by " / ". Marginal notes at right are three short references: AlIauhar., AlFiranz., Safioddin. (the second may read AlFiranz- with a line-end hyphen; treated as AlFiranz.). Long s rendered as s throughout. Printed "Ebn" and "Iorhamidæ" kept as printed.
